question: After the ______, Mahatma Gandhi called off the Non-Cooperation Movement.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **After the Chauri Chaura incident, Mahatma Gandhi **called off the** Non-Cooperation Movement**.
 
• **Chauri Chaura was a town in the state of Uttar Pradesh, India, where on February 4, 1922,** a group of protesters participating in the Non-Cooperation Movement clashed with police, resulting in the death of three policemen. In retaliation, the protesters set fire to a police station, killing 22 policemen who were inside.
 
• **Gandhi, who had been leading the Non-Cooperation Movement,** was deeply disturbed by the violent turn of events and called off the movement, as he believed that it had lost its nonviolent character.
